blocks.text: Organic compounds with the -CN functional group are alkanenitriles, e.g. ethanenitrile CH3CN and propanenitrile CH3CH2CN. Their preparation from halogenoalkanes and KCN was given in Chapter 21. The most important use of nitriles is their hydrolysis to carboxylic acids, which can be done with dilute acid or dilute alkali.

items: Acid hydrolysis: heating with dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid gives the carboxylic acid: CH3CN(aq) + 2H2O(l) + HCl(aq) -> CH3COOH(aq) + NH4Cl(aq).

Alkaline hydrolysis: heating with dilute sodium hydroxide gives the salt of the acid and ammonia, CH3CN(aq) + H2O(l) + NaOH(aq) -> CH3COONa(aq) + NH3(g); acidifying with dilute HCl releases the acid: CH3COONa(aq) + HCl(aq) -> CH3COOH(aq) + NaCl(aq).

blocks.prompt: What gas is given off when propanenitrile is heated with dilute sodium hydroxide, and what is the organic product?
blocks.explanation: Ammonia; sodium propanoate, CH3CH2COONa (which gives propanoic acid on acidification).

items: Nitriles RCN; made from RX + KCN (Chapter 21).
Acid hydrolysis: RCOOH + NH4Cl; alkaline: RCOONa + NH3, then acidify.
